build.note: Re-analysis of the 15 October 15-round TR-7 burst recordings (L4043); no new capture, game not launched.

question: Shot by shot, where does the TR-7 15-round burst diverge from the site law: is the climb convex as the close-up marks suggested (L4044), and where does the 15-round extent excess come from?

capture.note: Six clips, 18 bursts of 15 rounds (the HUD counter undercounted six of them), both suppressors, standing ADS with the SF G2 5.00x, 120 fps.

sourceFacts.method: camera-track.py: the world around the scope (the whole ADS frame is rendered at the scope magnification, 88.40 px/deg from the pairs lens scale) is registered frame to frame by gradient cross-correlation; the cumulative vertical shift is the camera pitch. Shots are placed on the fixed 83.3 ms cadence from the first detected kick; the pre-shot aim is the plateau before each kick, after the camera spring settles. Cross-check with a second crop; bursts kept when the crops agree within 0.3 deg at every shot. climb-video.py compares with predict-climb.mjs (mean pre-shot aim and 1 ms trace over 500 seeds). See ANALYSIS.md section 2b.

control.description: Two independent crops agree within 0.3 deg at every shot on 12 of 18 bursts; the detected kick cadence is 10 frames (83.3 ms) as stored; on the bursts whose end frame is a clean return to the start the chain drift is 0.1 to 0.4 deg; the first kick seen by the camera is 1.03 deg against the stored 1.16.

points: Pre-shot camera climb above shot 1, mean over the well-tracked bursts, minus the x0.8 law at shots 2 to 15: Standard [-0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.12, 0.19, 0.24, 0.34, 0.38, 0.32, 0.28, 0.29, 0.34, 0.28, 0.19] (7 bursts, 8.51 against 8.32 at shot 15; the stored law gives 7.40); Lightened [0.06, -0.02, 0.02, 0.07, 0.0, 0.04, -0.07, -0.25, -0.08, -0.11, -0.09, -0.03, -0.07, -0.01] (5 bursts, 7.61 against 7.62). First increment 0.91 / 0.98 against 0.93 / 0.92.

Fraction of pre-shot aims in the lower half of the shot-15 climb: 0.37 Standard, 0.36 Lightened, against 0.40 / 0.33 for the law: the climb is concave like the law. The convex reading from the close-up marks (L4044 section 2a) is withdrawn.

Spray top from the recovery frames where the camera is 3.3 deg above the start: 6.0 deg above the camera, i.e. about 9.3 to 9.6 deg above shot 1 in Standard C burst 0, against a shot-15 aim of 8.1 there and 8.5 on average; the model puts the top impact 0.35 above the aim. The close-up extents (11.2 / 9.6) are 1 to 2 deg above the video spray top.

Recovery after the 15th shot, climb above shot 1 at 200 / 300 / 400 / 500 ms, Standard: 6.44 / 3.46 / 0.75 / -0.28 against the x0.8 trace 5.21 / 1.79 / 0.27 / 0.00; Lightened 5.24 / 2.40 / 0.19 / -0.42 against 4.29 / 1.18 / 0.09 / 0.00. The camera descends at a near-constant 28 to 31 deg/s from 6.4 deg to 0.7 where the law runs at 37 falling to 10 deg/s.

Each kick is delivered over 3 frames (6 with the Lightened Suppressor, its 50 ms duration), overshoots, dips and settles on a plateau 7 to 9 frames after the onset; the camera-spring dip settles 0.36 to 0.46 deg above the pre-shot.

inference: The site law with the 0.8 scale reproduces the TR-7's pre-shot aim through a 15-round burst on both suppressors to within 0.4 deg; there is no late-burst excess in the aim. The 15-round extent excess is in the bullets' deviation from the aim (about 1 deg of extra upward scatter at the top of the spray) and the close-up extents overstate it by a further 1 to 2 deg. After the burst the recovery from 6 to 8 deg is rate-limited near 30 deg/s, which the pairs and the burst climb cannot see; this is the one place a structural change to the law is indicated by these data.
unresolved: The source of the extra upward impact deviation at high recoil (VerticalRecoilMin/Max 0.578 on this profile is the candidate operand); the post-burst undershoot of 0.3 to 0.4 deg at 500 ms (within the chain drift); the close-up extent method.
siteImpact: None applied; the x0.8 scale stands and the burst climb supports it. A recovery-rate limit near 30 deg/s would change only recovery after large displacements (long bursts followed by a pause) and needs a capture designed for it.

leads.title: TR-7 15-round burst videos, camera track: the pre-shot aim follows the x0.8 law to within 0.4 deg through all 15 shots on both suppressors (the convex-climb reading of L4044 is withdrawn); the extent excess is impact deviation above the aim; recovery after the burst is rate-limited near 30 deg/s
leads.summary: Frame-by-frame registration of the world around the scope in 18 bursts gives the camera pitch at 120 fps; the plateau before each kick is the pre-shot aim. Standard reaches 8.51 deg at shot 15 against 8.32 for the x0.8 law (stored 7.40), Lightened 7.61 against 7.62, every shot within 0.4 deg; lower-half fraction 0.37 / 0.36 against 0.40 / 0.33. The spray top sits 1.0 to 1.5 deg above the shot-15 aim (model 0.35), and the recovery after the last shot descends at a near-constant 28 to 31 deg/s where the law runs at 37 falling to 10.
leads.reopenWhen: A capture of long bursts followed by a held aim on two profiles (recovery-rate limit), or a mark-per-shot measurement of impact against aim (the upward deviation), or a readable implementation of the recoil kick and recovery.
